hook: The prophet who, in the Bible's story, led his people out of slavery in Egypt.

pages.x: In the Book of Exodus, a pharaoh orders every newborn Hebrew boy thrown into the Nile. One mother hides her son in a basket of reeds among the rushes, where Pharaoh's own daughter finds him. She names him Moses and raises him as an Egyptian prince.

Grown up, Moses kills an Egyptian he sees beating a Hebrew slave, and flees to the desert to work as a shepherd. On a mountain, God speaks to him from a bush that burns without burning up, and sends him back to Egypt to free his people.

Pharaoh refuses, and ten plagues strike Egypt: the Nile turns to blood, then come frogs, locusts, darkness and finally the death of every firstborn. Jews remember the escape that followed every year at Passover. Pursued by the Egyptian army, the Israelites cross the Red Sea as its waters part for them.

On Mount Sinai, Moses receives God's law, carved on two tablets of stone: worship one God, make no idols, keep the Sabbath, honour your father and mother, do not murder, steal, lie or envy. Around them grew the Torah, the law that has guided Jewish life ever since.

Moses leads the people through the wilderness for forty years. At the end, from the top of Mount Nebo, he is shown the Promised Land across the Jordan, but he dies before he can enter it. The Bible says no one knows where he is buried.

Historians debate whether Moses really lived, but his story is one of the most influential ever told. He is the greatest prophet of Judaism and honoured in Christianity and Islam; enslaved Americans sang "Go Down, Moses" and called Harriet Tubman their Moses.
pts: Led the Exodus from Egypt in the Bible
A prophet of Judaism, Christianity and Islam
